unharnessed.meaning: Every quantity, step and tip survives, with ingredients put in Australian terms: "plain flour", "bicarb soda", "chopped nuts, like peanuts", "swap two teaspoons of the white sugar for vanilla sugar". "dark choc bits" for semi-sweet is a fair local equivalent.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "not much chop to eat on its own", "bump up the spread", "baking paper", "Top-shelf butter, chocolate and vanilla will make a cracker of a bikkie", "rolled oats" for oatmeal.
unharnessed.authenticity: Reads like an Australian recipe written by a home cook: "Chuck in the vanilla and beat it through", "pop them in the 350°F oven", "On the flip side". Spelling localised: "flavour".
unharnessed.register: A friendly middle weight that suits level 3: casual verbs and local names, nothing piled on; no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the practical, encouraging recipe voice: "If you like a soft, squishy middle in your bikkie, pull them out one minute earlier".
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Let them sit for about 1 minute, then take them off the hot tray to cool on a wire rack."
unharnessed.variety: Varied verbs and turns ("Chuck in", "bump up", "tweak", "pop them in"), though "bikkies" is the noun in nearly every tip.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original recipe, sections and tips in order: "Notes, tips, and variations".

yarn.meaning: All quantities, steps and tips survive: "use two teaspoons of vanilla sugar in place of the same amount of white sugar", "the trick is to bump the flour up to 3+ cups". The first "Procedure" heading becomes "Method", so the recipe now has two "Method" sections.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "plain flour", "bicarb soda", "not much chop to eat on its own", "help rein in the spread", "baking paper". "won't spread out heaps" is fine.
yarn.authenticity: Natural Australian recipe English: "If you can't get hold of vanilla extract", "you mightn't like it in the bikkies either". "groundnuts" left unlocalised.
yarn.register: A light-to-middle weight, plain and local, suitable for level 3: "Top-quality butter, choccy and vanilla will make a better bikkie." No swearing.
yarn.tone: Keeps the practical recipe voice throughout: "just make sure the pieces are small enough to eat comfortably".
yarn.flow: Smooth throughout; switches between "biscuits" and "bikkies" sometimes in adjacent lines: "for thicker biscuits. The other way round, grease your tray if you like thinner (crispier) bikkies."
yarn.variety: Varied: "rein in", "bump the flour up", "not much chop", "get hold of".
yarn.essence: Clearly the original, every section and tip there.

engine.meaning: All content kept, mostly verbatim: "Cream butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar in a large mixer bowl."
engine.sense: Some swaps strain: "Some punters also recommend chilling dough" (punters are customers or gamblers, not people at large), "Using chopped bar choccy". Inconsistent localising: "plain flour" in the list but "Use cake flour instead of all-purpose", "chocolate morsels (chips)" left.
engine.authenticity: Mostly the original with word swaps; the cookie word varies at random: "chewier bickies", "crisper biscuits", "thinner bikkies", "a superior biscuit". Formal US recipe phrasing kept: "if you find this not to be the case".
engine.register: Lighter than level 3: most lines are untouched, such as "The proportion of granulated to brown sugar may be adjusted to suit taste."
engine.tone: The recipe's instructional tone is kept, as little is changed.
engine.flow: Readable, but the switching spellings jar: "More brown sugar will result in chewier bickies. More white sugar will result in crisper biscuits."
engine.essence: Recognisably the original recipe; it mostly is the original.

unharnessed.quote: More brown sugar makes chewier bikkies. More white sugar makes crispier bikkies.
unharnessed.original: More brown sugar will result in chewier cookies. More white sugar will result in crisper cookies.

yarn.quote: for thicker biscuits. The other way round, grease your tray if you like thinner (crispier) bikkies.
yarn.original: for thicker cookies. Conversely, grease your sheet if you like thinner (crispier) cookies.

engine.quote: Some punters also recommend chilling dough
engine.original: Some people also recommend chilling dough
engine.why: "punters" means customers or gamblers; an odd fit for people giving baking advice.

engine.quote: More brown sugar will result in chewier bickies. More white sugar will result in crisper biscuits.
engine.original: More brown sugar will result in chewier cookies. More white sugar will result in crisper cookies.

engine.quote: Use cake flour instead of all-purpose
engine.original: Use cake flour instead of all-purpose
engine.why: US "all-purpose" left after the list says "plain flour".

summaries.unharnessed: A natural, faithful Australian recipe at the right weight; "bikkies" is leaned on.
summaries.yarn: A faithful, natural local recipe, a touch plainer than A, with a duplicated heading.
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with word swaps, inconsistent and light, and one wrong-sense "punters".
